children: Saudi and Egyptian bourses fell on Sunday after the Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted drones and missiles over Riyadh and southern regions as fighting with Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis intensified.
dropped 2.6%, pressured by broad-based selling as investors assessed the risk of the Yemen conflict becoming a broader front in the regional war.

Outside the Gulf, Egypt's blue-chip index
tumbled 2.5%, eyeing its lowest level in nearly seven months, with all of its constituents in negative territory.

Egypt's parliament is expected to vote on October 26 on authorising the armed forces to support Saudi Arabia, if requested, in its conflict with Yemen's Houthis. The voting was initially scheduled for October 20.
